intro: PowerPoint for interior designers on Mac is the app you use for concept decks, mood boards and client presentations in Microsoft 365. The setup that saves the most time is one master template, a clear view of Design Suggestions limits, and a steady version routine. This guide covers each step, the limits that catch designers out, and where Lazur helps mid-slide.
tldr: Start every project from File > New from Template, then fix the master once.
Design Suggestions works only with built-in themes, on OneDrive or SharePoint files, and not on slides with shapes or text boxes.
Move slides to a new template with ⌘A and ⌘C, then right-click the thumbnail pane and paste with ⌘V.
Lazur points, explains and guides one click at a time. It does not click for you.

blocks.text: What interior designers build in PowerPoint on Mac

Most interior designers on a Mac use PowerPoint for the front end of a project. That means the concept deck, the mood board and the client presentation that sells the scheme. The specs and pricing often live somewhere else. Programa, a design management vendor, describes the common split in its client presentation guide. The concept deck sits in one app, the mood board in another, and the spec schedule in a spreadsheet. That is one vendor's view, so test it against your own work. The split is still worth planning for, because the deck is where the look gets decided.
Set up a master template before you open a client file

Start every project from a template, not from a blank file. In PowerPoint for Mac, choose File > New from Template, pick a template from the gallery, and click Create. That is Microsoft's own route. Once the file opens, spend your first session on the master, not the slides. Set the title placement, the fonts, the colors and the picture frames once. Every concept slide then starts from the same place.

Think about what you repeat on every project. That usually means a cover, a section divider, a photo grid, a material board and a closing slide with your contact details. Build each one as a layout in the master. Name the layouts clearly, so you can find them when a client asks for a change late in the day.
One trade-off comes early. Design Suggestions only works with built-in themes. A custom or downloaded theme gets no layout help. Decide that at the start, not three weeks in.
Order of work for a new master

items: Pick a built-in theme if you want Design Suggestions to help with layouts.
Open View > Slide Master and set the title, body and picture placeholders.
Set fonts and colors once, then check them on a second screen or a projector.
Save the file to OneDrive or SharePoint so the layout tools can run.
Duplicate the master for each project, then rename the file with the client name and date.

blocks.text: If a menu name looks different on your copy, look in the View menu first. Your build may be older or newer than the one this page describes. For the full master steps, see [How to edit the slide master in PowerPoint on Mac](/how-to/edit-the-slide-master-in-powerpoint).
Move slides onto a new template without rebuilding them

Clients change their minds. A concept may need a new brand, a new palette or a new template. Do not rebuild the slides by hand. Microsoft's method works on a Mac. Open the source deck and press ⌘A to select every slide. Press ⌘C to copy them. Open the new template file, right-click the thumbnail pane on the left, and press ⌘V. The pasted slides take the new template's design.

Check the result before you trust it. Look at font sizes, picture crops and captions after the paste. A change of template can change how things sit on the slide. Ten minutes per deck is a fair budget for the check, and a deck full of photos needs more time.

blocks.title: Paste a few slides first
blocks.text: Copy three or four slides, paste them into the new template, and check them. If the result is wrong, undo with ⌘Z and try a different layout before you paste the whole deck.
Use Design Suggestions for layouts, and learn its limits

Microsoft renamed Designer to Design Suggestions. The feature watches the content on a slide and offers layout ideas. It can arrange pictures, charts and tables. It can turn text lists, processes or timelines into SmartArt. It can also add illustrations for key terms. For interior work, the picture layouts matter most. A set of photos for a mood board can get a tidy arrangement from one suggestion.

The feature is strict, and Microsoft lists its limits. It needs a Microsoft 365 subscription. On Mac, it works only for files stored on OneDrive and SharePoint. Read the table before you plan a deck around it.

headers: What it means for your deck
rows: A custom or downloaded theme gets no suggestions.
Use the Title or Title + Content layout, with no extra shapes.
Up to four photos, each larger than 200 x 200 pixels.
A slide with shapes or text boxes gets no suggestions.
Suggestions are withheld when several people edit the same slide.
Works only for files on OneDrive or SharePoint on Mac.
blocks.caption: Design Suggestions limits from Microsoft's support page.

blocks.text: Plan the slide order around those limits. If you want suggestions on a photo slide, place the pictures first and keep that slide free of extra shapes. Add labels and annotations once the layout is set.
To turn suggestions off, go to Preferences > General and clear Automatically show me design ideas. Your slides stay as they are. You only lose the prompts.
Why the Design Suggestions button is missing or greyed out

A grey button usually has a simple cause. Microsoft lists the main ones. The button is unavailable when you are offline. It is also unavailable when no single slide is selected, when the Notes pane has focus, or when you are in Slide Show view. A missing button has a bigger cause. Your build may be older than the Microsoft 365 version, or an administrator may have turned the feature off.

items: Offline: reconnect, then select the slide again.
No single slide selected: click one thumbnail, not a group.
Notes pane has focus: click the slide itself.
Slide Show view: press Esc to leave the show, then try again.
Older build or admin setting: check your version, then ask whoever manages your Microsoft 365 license.

blocks.text: Mood boards and icons: image rules that save rework

Mood boards are image heavy, so two things go wrong. The first is file size. The second is placement. Size your pictures before you add them. Picture slides allow no more than four photos, and each photo must be larger than 200 x 200 pixels. Keep the full-resolution originals in a folder, and place a smaller copy in the deck if the file grows too big.

Icons are the second rule. PowerPoint for Mac supports SVG natively from version 16.13. Since version 16.107, dated March 10, 2026, Mac stops saving a PNG fallback for each SVG. If a client opens the deck in an older version, check that the icons still show before you send it.

Add alt text to every photo. It helps screen readers and keeps the deck clear when a file is shared. The steps are in [How to add alt text to an image in PowerPoint on Mac](/how-to/add-alt-text-to-an-image-in-powerpoint).
Client presentations: versions, PDFs and prices that drift

A price in a deck is a risk. Programa calls retyping 'manual re-entry'. Each time you type a price, finish or product code again, a number can drift from the spreadsheet. The same guide says designers send PDFs, and clients then reply about older versions. It does not put a figure on that. The fix is still simple to describe.

Keep one source of truth for prices and finishes. Copy numbers into the deck only at the final pass. Name each version by date and stage, such as Kitchen_concept_v3_2026-11-09. Export a PDF only from the final version. Write the version number on the cover slide, so a question about an old file takes seconds to answer.

Read those numbers with care. A 2025 Kantar study, shared by a vendor that sells PowerPoint add-ins, is the source. The sample was US office employees, not interior designers. The 6.5 hours is a PowerPoint-only figure. Treat it as a rough signal, not a measure of your studio. The rebuild habit is the useful part. If you rebuild similar decks from memory, the master and the version routine above will help most.
Speed up a PowerPoint for Mac file that slows down

Big decks slow down, and interior decks are often big. A Microsoft Q&A thread describes one user on PowerPoint for Mac 16.97 with macOS Sequoia 15.5. After 20 to 30 minutes, every edit lagged for several seconds. The deck had 50 to 100 slides, PNG graphics and high-quality background images. Only a restart fixed it. That build is old, and the thread has no confirmed fix. Treat it as one report, not a rule.
Try the thread's suggestions in this order, and stop when the lag stops.

items: Update PowerPoint and macOS to the latest versions.
Turn off add-ins under Tools > Templates and Add-ins.
Run File > Reduce File Size on a copy of the deck.
Clear the cache and restart PowerPoint during long sessions.
Test the deck in Safe Mode to see whether an add-in or the file is the cause.

blocks.title: Back up before you shrink
blocks.text: Run File > Reduce File Size on a copy, not on your master. Then check the photos and backgrounds, because a shrunk file can look different from the original.
Check your PowerPoint build and Microsoft's known issues

Know your build number before you troubleshoot. Microsoft's release notes list 16.114.3, build 26102720, dated Oct 27, 2026, as the latest Mac release. That entry covers quality and performance only. The notes from September and October 2026 show no changes to Designer, templates or the ribbon. The latest feature change in the notes is Copilot in PowerPoint, from version 16.109 on May 12, 2026.

Copilot can create, edit and refine a presentation from a prompt. It keeps formatting and branding in place. On Copilot Premium, you also get brand kit templates, brand-approved images and brand compliance checks. If your studio already keeps a brand kit, test it on one project before you change how you work.

blocks.title: Check your license first
blocks.text: Microsoft's known-issues page says that from July 13, 2026, some Microsoft 365 subscribers on macOS can open and print files but cannot edit, save or create new files. The page calls this reduced functionality mode. The entry does not clearly say which licenses it covers, so check with Microsoft before a deadline.
What Microsoft 365 costs for a one-person studio

Design Suggestions needs a Microsoft 365 subscription, so budget for it. Microsoft lists US prices on its buy page. Prices may vary by region, so check the page for your country before you commit. The table below uses US list prices only.

blocks.caption: US list prices from Microsoft's buy page.

blocks.text: Choose the plan by who needs the files, not by the app list alone. A one-person studio usually starts with Personal. If you share the plan with other people, compare both plans on Microsoft's page. This page does not list every feature of each plan, so read the details there.
Where Lazur fits in a PowerPoint session

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It lives in the notch at the top of your screen. Hold ⌥ ⌘, Option and Command together, and ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and it draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for PowerPoint. It has no partnerships with any app maker. Think of it as a sharp friend beside you. It points, explains and waits. Your hands do the work.

Dictation is a separate feature. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. That helps when you write spec notes or speaker notes. Snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots help with the words you type every week, such as finish names and supplier codes. See [PowerPoint help with Lazur](/apps/powerpoint) for the slide-specific side.
Mistakes that cost interior designers time in PowerPoint

items: Building on a custom theme, then wondering why Design Suggestions does nothing.
Pasting slides into a new template and skipping the check afterward.
Adding text boxes to a photo slide, then losing suggestions on that slide.
Retyping prices and finishes in the deck instead of copying from one source.
Sending PDFs with no version number, then answering questions about old files.
Leaving add-ins on through a long session, then blaming the app when it slows.

blocks.text: Most of these come from a deck that grew without a plan. A master, a version name and one price source help with most of them. The routine below covers all three.
A file routine for each client project
Here is a routine that keeps the deck quick and the numbers honest. Run it once for each project. The setup takes little time, and it saves rework later in the job.

items: Start from File > New from Template, or from your studio master.
Save the project to OneDrive or SharePoint so Design Suggestions can run.
Build the picture slides first, using the Title or Title + Content layout.
Add text boxes and labels last, after the layout is settled.
Copy prices and finish codes from the spreadsheet only at the final pass.
Export a PDF from the final version, and write the version number on the cover.

Pick one small project and run the routine on it. Start with a single concept deck, not your biggest client job. Notice where the master, the template move and the final export slow you down. Then keep the steps that help and drop the rest.

faq.question: Is there a PowerPoint template for interior designers on Mac?
faq.answer: Start with Microsoft's gallery. Choose File > New from Template, pick a template, and click Create. Then edit the master to match your studio. This page does not name a third-party template, so compare any template with your own layouts before you buy one.

faq.question: Why does Design Suggestions not appear on my PowerPoint for Mac file?
faq.answer: Microsoft's notes point to a few causes. The file may be stored locally instead of on OneDrive or SharePoint. The theme may be custom, or a slide may hold shapes or text boxes. Your build may also be older. If the button is still missing, your administrator may have turned the feature off.

faq.question: Can I use my studio's brand theme with Design Suggestions?
faq.answer: Not directly. Design Suggestions works only with built-in themes, not custom or downloaded ones. If your brand matters more than layout help, build the master on your own theme and place layouts by hand. Decide this before the project starts.

faq.question: How much does Microsoft 365 cost on a Mac?
faq.answer: US list prices are $99.99 per year or $9.99 per month for Microsoft 365 Personal. Family is $129.99 per year or $12.99 per month. Prices vary by region, so check Microsoft's buy page for your country.

faq.question: Does Lazur edit my slides or click through PowerPoint for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at things, explains them out loud and guides you one click at a time. It drafts and types text when you ask. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you.

faq.question: Does Lazur see my client files?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Is Lazur a PowerPoint add-in?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnerships with any app maker. It is a voice assistant that runs on your Mac alongside PowerPoint.

faq.question: Why is my PowerPoint for Mac file slow?
faq.answer: Large decks with many photos and high-quality backgrounds can lag. Update PowerPoint and macOS, turn off add-ins under Tools > Templates and Add-ins, run File > Reduce File Size on a copy, and restart after long sessions.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows too?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.
